messages:
ashley: Heads up — overnight we saw a burst of NVIDIA Xid 13 and 31 on rack-a10-07. ~40 faults between 03:12–03:32 UTC, health dashboard flagged ECC correction rate spike. I pulled live jobs off the rack and routed traffic away.
infra-bot: ALERT: gpu-error-rate increase on rack-a10-07 (codes: Xid 13, Xid 31). Severity: warning. Link: https://console/redwood/infra/alerts/INFRA-1422 :warning:
raj: Which workloads were on the rack? decode/encoder/embeddings?
ashley: Mostly stream-decode (decoder-only) and high-throughput embedder. Batch sizes small (1-2), seq lengths ~1k. A few bursty low-latency tenants too.
eva: I grabbed logs from the nodes. nvidia-driver logs show lots of kernel-timeout traces tied to Xid 13 and some ECC single-bit correction counters climbing. Snippet:
```
[2026-03-17T03:14:05Z] Xid 13 at GPU 1: GPU hang during kernel execution
[2026-03-17T03:14:06Z] ECC errors corrected on GPU 1: ce_count=124 -> 141
[2026-03-17T03:18:02Z] Xid 31 at GPU 1: PCIe link error reported
```
sam: Also saw a small bump in TCP retransmits from that rack around 03:10–03:20, could be unrelated but worth checking. increased pod restarts for embedder service at the same time.
raj: Could be a NIC interrupt storm causing scheduler latencies, which then surface as GPU kernel timeouts. What driver + firmware versions on those hosts?
ashley: Drivers: NVIDIA 545.89, CUDA runtime 12.3, host firmware last applied 2025-09-10. All racks on the same batch.
eva: Further log detail: Xid 31 entries often co-occur with PCIe AER messages. Example:
```
[03:17:58] pcieport 0000:3e:00.0: AER: Corrected error received: id=00e0 unrec=0
[03:17:58] Xid 31: RX ECC? pcie link flaps
```
ashley: Immediate mitigation: I ran `kubectl drain gpu-rack-a10-07-03 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` and moved tenants to a10-08. Plan is to cold-swap suspect card in slot 2 after noon if repro persists.
raj: Can we reproduce in a controlled way? Suggest running the same small-batch decode workload and then a mem/stress test. If we cannot repro, might be transient link issue.
eva: I queued two reproducer runs: (1) embedder small-batch, seq=1024, batch=1, 1h; (2) `cuda-memtest` for 30m. Also enabling pcie AER counters via `setpci` and extra kernel logging. I'll post results.
sam: Note on routing — shifting embedder traffic to a10-08 will increase burst cost by ~12% for the day. OK for now but flagging finance.
ashley: Good. If reproducer hits Xid again, escalate to vendor for RMA. If only PCIe AER shows up, we'll try reseating cable and checking switch logs. If driver bug suspected, we can test rolling to 550+ driver on a single node.
infra-bot: Ticket created: INFRA-1422 — "rack-a10-07 intermittent Xid13/Xid31 cluster". Replacement window proposed 2026-03-17 13:00 UTC. Assigned: ashley (owner), eva (logs), raj (network), sam (routing).
raj: One more ask — can someone share the tenant list impacted so SRE oncall can post status updates? I can prepare fallback routes for high-SLO tenants.
ashley: Posted a quick tenant mapping in the ticket. High-SLO tenants: payments-api, realtime-embeds. I've configured canary throttles so payments traffic stays on host a10-08 only.
eva: Reproducer run 1: 14m in, saw first Xid 13 on GPU 1 at iteration 82. Attaching stacktrace in ticket. We're seeing consistent repro with the decoder workload.
ashley: OK that pushes this towards hardware/kernel scheduling issue. Next steps: schedule RMA for the GPU if reseat doesn't fix it. I'll coordinate with vendor.
sam: Thx all — monitoring dashboard lowered alert threshold to 5 errors/min and set a temporary mute window for noisy metrics while we replace.
ashley: Closing actions for now: keep rack drained, don't place critical SLO tenants back until RMA or pass 24h repro-free. I'll update INFRA-1422 after the vendor call. :white_check_mark:
